title: Sort Products by Profit Margin
description:
Write a query that returns `id`, `name`, `price`, `cost`, and the profit (`price - cost`) as `profit`. Sort the results by `profit` **descending** so the most profitable product appears first.

**Table: products**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| price | DECIMAL |
| cost | DECIMAL |
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, cost DECIMAL); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1, 'Laptop', 999.99, 750.00), (2, 'Phone', 699.99, 400.00), (3, 'Tablet', 449.99, 300.00), (4, 'Watch', 299.99, 100.00), (5, 'Earbuds', 149.99, 80.00), (6, 'Charger', 29.99, 5.00);
solution_sql: SELECT id, name, price, cost, (price - cost) AS profit FROM products ORDER BY (price - cost) DESC

test_cases.description: Returns 6 products ordered by profit descending

hints: You can use an arithmetic expression directly in `ORDER BY` — or reference the alias defined in `SELECT`.
Phone profit (699.99 - 400 = 299.99) beats Laptop profit (999.99 - 750 = 249.99), so Phone ranks first.
explanation: `ORDER BY (price - cost) DESC` computes the profit on the fly and sorts largest profit first. Phone ($299.99) > Laptop ($249.99) > Watch ($199.99) > Tablet ($149.99) > Earbuds ($69.99) > Charger ($24.99).
